result.title: SlideJev: Order-Stable and Tissue-Grounded Jev Decisions for Whole-Slide Pathology
result.summary: Whole-slide visual question answering (VQA) offers a natural-language interface to pathology, allowing diagnostic and phenotypic questions to be answered directly from tissue slides. However, current vision-language models (VLMs) rely heavily on linguistic priors: their answers are sensitive to the order of the candidate answers, and can be reached through shortcuts that bypass the tissue evidence. To address these challenges, we introduce SlideJev, a framework that separately verifies candidate answers against the slide and learns to ground these judgments in tissue evidence. To connect parallel candidate evaluation with visual evidence learning, we adopt Jev and score each candidate by the difference between support and rejection log-likelihoods from the original language-model head. We compute these scores in parallel using separate prompts with the same format and no option-position labels, then normalize them for answer selection. To ground these scores in tissue evidence, candidate-conditioned reading and comparison guide gated updates to visual tokens across decoder layers. With the backbone frozen, we train these visual modules through the same scores using question-answer and paired-image supervision. Across three whole-slide pathology VQA benchmarks, SlideJev achieves the highest mean overall accuracy and 100% answer consistency across four option orders. Image-control experiments further show that SlideJev achieves the largest average accuracy gains from correct images over mismatched and image-free inputs across the three datasets. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/leowu-ai/SlideJev.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 SlideJev，用 Jev 分别计算各候选答案的支持与拒绝对数似然差并并行评估，同时以候选条件化的视觉 token 门控更新，将判断绑定到全切片组织证据上。
AI.relevance_reason: 其针对选项顺序敏感和绕过组织证据的捷径，正对应 VLM 推理中答案是否真正使用视觉内容与视觉旁路问题，可供核查其证据门控与并行候选验证机制。
